newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Trotman welcomes strengthening yen.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Trotman welcomes strengthening yen.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Chairman Alex Trotman said Friday the recent strengthening of the yen was good news and thought the trend would continue.
"From my point of view, as a very major manufacturer in dollars, I regard that as good news," Trotman told reporters.

He was attending a meeting of the Business Council, a group of the nation's top corporate executives, and spoke to reporters following a closed-door speech to the group by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
The Big Three American car manufacturers have been among the most vocal of U.S. industries that have expressed alarm about the strength of the dollar against the Japanese yen.
Trotman said that each yen change has a "huge" impact on the bottom line of U.S. car manufacturers.
"I am feeling a little optimistic that with what we have been hearing ... that our voice is being heard," Trotman said.

The yen strengthened from about 123 per dollar on Thursday to around 120 yen on Friday after comments by Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara that it was theoretically possible the dollar/yen could strengthen to 103 yen.

"I think that as a result of the things that have been said over the last few weeks, we are seeing some strengthening and I personally think that (the strengthening yen) is going to continue," Trotman said.

He said that it had been suggested during the morning closed-door discussions that Japanese manufacturers could be competitive at 110 yen. But Trotman said the best Japanese car manufacturers would "still be in comfortable territory" at 110 yen. Japanese car manufacturers could be competitive with the yen/dollar ratio at 100, he said.
